title: Platform Engineering and IDPs in 2026
body:
Platform Engineering has become the fastest-growing discipline in cloud infrastructure, with Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs) now standard at organisations employing more than 200 engineers. The platform team builds and operates the "paved road" — the self-service layer that lets application developers provision infrastructure, deploy services, and manage environments without directly touching Kubernetes YAML or cloud consoles. The role is structurally different from traditional DevOps: platform engineers are a product team whose internal customers are other engineers, and they are measured by developer experience and platform adoption rather than application uptime.

The core IDP stack in 2026 combines Backstage (CNCF developer portal) for the service catalog and self-service scaffolding, Crossplane or Terraform for infrastructure provisioning, ArgoCD or Flux for GitOps-based continuous delivery, and the LGTM stack (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir) for observability. Platform engineers design these systems and then abstract them into golden paths that application teams consume without needing deep infrastructure knowledge. The Crossplane Composition pattern is particularly important: it lets platform engineers expose a simple AppDatabase custom resource that provisions a fully configured cloud database (RDS, Cloud SQL, or Azure Flexible Server) from a single Kubernetes manifest, hiding the underlying provider complexity.

The certification stack most aligned with Platform Engineering responsibilities in 2026 is: CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator) as the highest-priority credential, Terraform Associate (003) for infrastructure-as-code depth, CKAD (Certified Kubernetes Application Developer) to understand the developer-facing Kubernetes surface, and GitHub Foundations for the CI/CD and automation layer. KCNA (Kubernetes and Cloud Native Associate) is a useful entry-level stepping stone for engineers transitioning from adjacent roles. Hiring managers at companies with active IDP programmes look for the CKA + Terraform combination as the minimum credentialling bar for mid-level roles.

Salaries for Platform Engineers in 2026 reflect the breadth of skills and direct impact the role has on engineering productivity. Mid-level Platform Engineers with CKA and Terraform Associate earn $145,000–$190,000 in major US technology markets. Senior platform architects holding CKA, CKAD, and a cloud specialty certification exceed $200,000, with principal-level roles at growth-stage technology companies reaching $280,000 in total compensation including equity. The highest-compensated platform engineering roles are not those with the deepest technical expertise alone — they are the roles that combine Kubernetes depth with product thinking and measurable developer experience improvement.
